review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Southern California and western North Atlantic archival tagging support SST use; vertical dive depth is not seafloor bathymetry.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 2 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for common thresher shark.
factors.value_notes: Southern California archival tags (57 deployed, 4 recovered) recorded use of waters with SST 16-21 °C. A 2025 western North Atlantic study of 48 tagged threshers found a broad -0.5 to 25.6 °C range, with about 90% of time in 14-20 °C water. This supports the configured 14-21 °C / 16-19 °C band as broad thermal context, but sample sizes, regions and seasonal behavior differ; it is not a universal catch-probability curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for common thresher shark.
factors.value_notes: Archival tags show common threshers move through the water column from the surface to at least 320 m in Southern California and up to much greater depths in western North Atlantic records. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not shark vertical dive depth; the configured 0-150 m seabed band is only a weak shelf/offshore context proxy, not a preferred bottom-depth interval.
